intent: Check per-address reverse-DNS authority and plan eligibility; not a provider ranking, SMTP-unblocking tutorial or forward-DNS migration.
productFit: A documented requirement to verify while choosing a suitable VPS. Does not reposition the main cheap-VPS site or invent prices.
dataRationale: Actual GSC includes VPS buying, address, bandwidth and feature-limit queries, but no direct PTR demand is claimed. Small organic samples justify a narrowly scoped assistance guide, not a traffic forecast.

competitorGap.observation: Hetzner separates domain-zone records from provider-managed rDNS and shows its own controls. New guide converts that into a provider-neutral authority checklist.
DigitalOcean documents name-based PTR handling and specific IPv6 constraints. New guide asks about each assigned address instead of copying one universal dashboard recipe.
AWS Elastic-IP reverse-DNS instructions have a matching-forward-A prerequisite. New guide explicitly treats this as one provider example, not a rule for every VPS.

cannibalizationCheck.method: Read all main articles and queued slugs/gaps, with focused body search for reverse DNS/PTR and actual GSC query-page rows.

nearby.distinction: Email eligibility mentions reverse DNS briefly; this new article focuses on reverse-zone control and per-address verification, without becoming a mail-delivery checklist.
Reputation/remediation is a separate question; a PTR does not settle it.
Forward website cutover, caches and rollback differ from control of address-to-name reverse records.

cannibalizationCheck.decision: Create one separate authority-focused guide, retaining historical URLs and future approved drafts.

originalExample: node.example.com and RFC5737 documentation address203.0.113.10, forward A vs reverse PTR diagram; example dig commands explicitly not executed, no output fabricated.
